title: The Merchant's Secret Iron Safe (TA)
summary: A paranoid merchant builds an impenetrable iron vault, only to lock himself inside. Birbal saves the miser and reveals the prison of greed.
full_text:
A fabulously wealthy diamond merchant of Agra named Seth Dinanath was so terrified of thieves that he spent five thousand gold coins commissioning the master imperial blacksmith to build a colossal iron safe inside his cellar. The safe had walls four inches thick, three massive combination locks, and spring-loaded steel bolts that snapped shut automatically.

Every evening, the merchant unlocked the heavy iron door, stepped inside his vault, closed the door behind him, and counted his diamond trays by the light of a single candle.

One evening, while inside the safe, the merchant accidentally brushed against the door frame. The heavy steel door swung shut with a thunderous *CLANG!*

The spring-loaded bolts snapped into place. The door locked automatically from the outside!

The merchant shrieked in mortal terror! The key was in his pocket, but the keyhole was only on the outside of the door! The walls were soundproof, and the air inside the sealed iron box would last for barely three hours!

He banged his fists against the iron, but no sound escaped to the floor above.

Fortunately, Birbal happened to visit the merchant's mansion that evening to collect an imperial charity donation. Hearing the merchant's frantic wife crying that her husband had vanished in the cellar, Birbal rushed down to the vault.

Birbal noticed the locked safe and smelled the faint smoke of an extinguished candle seeping through a tiny seam.

Birbal realized the merchant was suffocating inside!

There was no time to fetch locksmiths. Birbal ordered two blacksmiths with heavy sledgehammers and cold chisels to smash the external brass hinge pin. Working frantically, they sheared off the hinge, pried open the door with an iron lever, and dragged the unconscious, gasping merchant out into the fresh air!

After drinking cold water and catching his breath, Dinanath wept with gratitude, clutching Birbal's feet: 'You saved my life! My own safe nearly became my iron coffin!'

Birbal looked at the dark, suffocating vault with profound solemnity:

'Sethji, your safe was already your coffin long before the door snapped shut!

'A man who lives in constant terror, distrusting his neighbors, locking his wealth in the dark, and starving his spirit of generosity is a living corpse trapped in the prison of his own avarice.

'If you wish to be truly safe, unlock your heart, invest your wealth in public wells, schools, and hospitals, and the prayers of thousands will protect you better than four inches of solid iron!'

The merchant was transformed by the near-death experience. He melted down the iron safe, distributed half his wealth to the poor of Agra, and lived the rest of his days in peaceful freedom.
moral: நீதி மற்றும் வாழ்க்கை பாடம்: Wit beats power
